title: Add model capability & performance profile schema to public model metadata API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When teams onboard models to Redwood we currently surface only a small set of model metadata (name, description, default_version). Product and customer teams have requested an official, structured API schema to publish model capabilities and performance profiles (limits, context window, supported features, and recommended configs) so SDKs, the Console, and router policies can make automated decisions (pinning, fallbacks, routing by cost/latency).

Proposed solution: introduce a ModelProfile resource exposed via the model metadata API. Backwards-compatible: existing model metadata endpoints continue to work; profiles are additive and opt-in for model publishers. Core endpoints: 1) GET /v1/models/{model_id}/profile 2) GET /v1/models?include_profiles=true 3) POST /v1/models/{model_id}/profile (internal/publisher only)

Canonical profile schema (human-readable example below, actual transport is JSON):
- model_id (string)
- profile_version (semver string)
- published_at (ISO date)
- signed_digest (hex) -- optional, for trust
- recommended_pin (string) -- version id to default-pin for hosted usage
- context_window: {max_input_tokens, max_total_tokens} -- flattened in schema as max_input_tokens, max_total_tokens
- limits: ["max_tokens_per_request","requests_per_minute","concurrent_streams"] (integers)
- features: ["streaming","function_calling","structured_output","embeddings","multimodal"] (list of supported capabilities)
- performance_profiles: list of strings with names (see performance_* fields below)
- default_performance_profile: string
- performance_<profile_name>_latency_p50_ms, performance_<profile_name>_latency_p95_ms, performance_<profile_name>_tokens_per_sec, performance_<profile_name>_recommended_batch_size, performance_<profile_name>_quantization_modes (arrays) -- flattened numeric/string fields in the returned JSON to keep the schema easy to parse for older SDKs
- compatibility_tags: list (eg: ["kv-cache-v2","attn-optim-1","bfloat16-safe"])
- fallback_models: list (model ids)
- deprecation_date: ISO date or empty

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Flattened numeric fields for performance profiles: reduces parsing complexity in older SDKs but may lead to sparse keys when many profiles exist. We will limit number of published profiles to 3 to control payload size.
- Opt-in publishing: model publishers must explicitly POST a profile. This avoids accidental breaking changes for models that are still being evaluated.
- Signed digest is optional to allow internal pilot without HSM initially; long-term we will require signed profiles for private deployments.
- Version pinning semantics: recommended_pin is advisory. The router will implement a "pin-if-supported" policy: if a customer has requested version pinning, router will attempt to route to the pinned version; if unavailable, it will fall back using fallback_models or the default model variant with best matching compatibility_tags.

SDK and Console implications:
- SDKs: add ModelProfile class, new method get_model_profile(model_id) and include_profiles=true flag on list_models. Default SDK behavior: do not fetch profiles unless explicitly requested to preserve latency.
- Console: show a "profiles" tab on model detail page, allow toggling published profile versions, and expose a performance profile explorer that maps workload to recommended profile.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal pilot): support profile POST/GET on internal staging only. Update onboarding docs and create a Confluence checklist for model publishers.
- Phase 2 (beta): enable read-only GET on hosted API for all customers; publishers in a whitelisted org can POST profiles. SDKs updated to surface model profiles behind a flag.
- Phase 3 (general availability): public POST allowed for verified publishers; console editor enabled; profiles used by routing and Canary rollouts.

Operational/Monitoring:
- Add a dashboard metric: profile_fetch_success_rate, profile_cache_hit_rate, and profile_invalidation_events.
- Alert: >5% profile fetch errors for 1h will page platform-oncall.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

- Prototype UI mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mQx-example-mocks
- Backend PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4271
- SDK change PR (wip): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/912
acceptance_criteria: Profile GET returns documented flattened schema for a sample model and includes performance metrics for at least one profile
SDKs can opt-in to fetch profiles and parse flattened performance keys without errors
Console shows profile tab with ability to select a published profile version
Router reads recommended_pin and default_performance_profile when present and falls back safely when not
Monitoring dashboards show profile fetch and cache metrics
test_plan: Unit tests for profile serialization/deserialization covering nested->flattened transformation
Integration test: onboard a test model, POST profile to staging, GET profile from SDK and verify fields
Load test: 10k profile GETs per minute with 95th percentile latency < 120ms from edge cache
Backward compatibility test: old SDK that doesn't request profiles must receive no new required fields
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal staging pilot with 2 publisher teams (expect feedback)
Week 2: beta read-only GET to all customers, monitor errors and payload size
Week 3-4: enable whitelisted POST and console editor; update onboarding docs and run a publisher workshop
Week 5: GA with public POST and runtime using profiles for routing (feature flag gated)
migration_notes: For model publishers: create and POST a first profile using the onboarding checklist. For SDK consumers: add an opt-in flag (fetch_model_profiles=true) before calling list_models to avoid additional latency. Ensure client caches profiles for up to 5 minutes; invalidation is driven by profile_version and published_at. Internal router will ignore unknown keys to remain forward compatible.
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial spec drafted after sync with PM (R. Alvarez) and Runtime team. Decided on flattened perf keys to reduce SDK changes.

2026-03-05: Security ping: S. Malik reviewed and flagged private-deploy requirement for signed profiles; agreed to optional signed_digest for hosted GA, mandatory for private deployments. Refer to internal ticket ENG-7748 for HSM integration.
2026-03-06: Backend PR #4271 opened (draft). Initial endpoints and DB schema (profiles table) implemented. Pending performance field shape finalization.

2026-03-09: SDK PR #912 opened by SDK team, requested API ergonomics changes: prefer getModelProfile(modelId) over listModels(includeProfiles). Decided to implement both but keep include_profiles as server-side optimization flag.
2026-03-10: Load test planning. Assigned to infra perf team (Marcus Chen). Target: profile GET p95 < 120ms from CDN cache.
